report.answer_text:
Solar Orbiter captured the first clear images of the Sun’s south pole in March 2025. Its magnetic maps revealed patches of both north and south magnetic polarity side by side, rather than one dominant polarity. ESA released the images on June 11, 2025. (esa.int)
That patchwork is characteristic of solar maximum, the active phase of the Sun’s roughly 11-year cycle when its global magnetic field reverses. (esa.int)
